newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria increased exports, cut imports in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Syria increased exports, cut imports in 1995.

text.p: The value of Syrian exports rose by nearly 12 percent and imports fell by almost 14 percent in 1995 compared with 1994, according to an official report issued recently by the Central Bureau of Statistics.
The value of exports rose to 44.5 billion Syrian pounds from 39.8 billion. Imports fell to 52.8 billion pounds from 61.3 billion.
The bureau made the calculations at the official rate of 11.2 pounds to a U.S. dollar. The black market rate is 50 pounds to the dollar.
Syria imports mainly machinery, transportation equipment and manufactured and partly manufactured goods.
It exports more than half its daily crude oil production of around 600,000 barrels. Non-oil exports are cotton, textiles, phosphate, wheat and cereals.
Imports from Japan dropped to 2.3 billion pounds from 6.2 billion in 1994, when it was the biggest supplier to Syria. In 1995 it became the fifth.
Exports to Italy dropped to 10.4 billion pounds from 10.7 billion, yet it remained the biggest market for Syrian exports.
Imports from Italy, still the second largest supplier, fell to 3.9 billion pounds from 5.3 billion in 1994.
The biggest supplier in 1995 was Germany, with exports worth 5.5 billion pounds versus 5.2 billion the year before.
The United States increased exports slightly to 3.57 billion pounds from 3.53 billion and was the third biggest supplier.
French imports rose to 6.4 billion pounds from 4.9 billion. It was the second biggest market for Syrian goods.
The third biggest market was Spain, which increased imports to 3.4 billion pounds from 2.7 billion.
Exports to Turkey rose to 2.5 billion pounds from 0.9 billion. Turkey became the fifth biggest market.
